rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
Ritual / practice (noun) / ceremony — hard ban
No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
Register match.
Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The target is an AE101 lecture, not an article draft.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: visible timing inside a lecture turns trainer pacing into student prose and makes the slide cadence feel prescribed; that harm is present at raw line 20: "A 30-second move first." The rule's timing-location sub-rule puts lecture timing below the maintainer cut. Credit itself passes: Dex Horthy is named at raw line 35, and the maintainer block records the deliberate Pocock attribution placement.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Keep the optional move's low-cost signal without a numeric duration in the lecture body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
Over-hedge detector.
Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The target is the student-facing lecture, not the reference artefact that holds a user-supplied frame for comparison.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
Watch out for planting jargon too early.
Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
Standard shape for the `**What happened:**` block — three moves.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The lecture has no `What happened` recap block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
Earn every technical term on first use.
Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is AE101 for software engineers, not the Agents 101 business audience.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The body does not use memory or context as curriculum concepts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The body does not ask Claude to produce a student artefact with a prescribed output structure; fenced prompt content is outside writing-class scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module. Compound-shape varies per module — never repeat same Debrief.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The lecture has no Debrief or compound-retro interview.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The target is a lecture, not a simulation protocol.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The body does not name or write a CLAUDE.md file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The student-facing body contains no inline markdown links.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The lecture does not ask the student to author a contested rule, memory, skill, plan, agent, or subagent artefact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
Session / task / run split (all trainings).
No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: cadence-specific time language becomes false when modules run back-to-back, on separate weeks, or in a two-day intensive; that harm is present at raw line 16: "Not today, but soon." A later multi-session beat can occur on the same calendar day.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Keep the forward hint, but make it module-relative or remove the time phrase.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
No meta-ask when student has already decided.
`.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The body does not direct Claude or the student to save a new text artefact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm checked: generic read/watch instructions narrate the action already happening and add patronizing cognitive load; that harm is present at raw line 27: "Watch what comes back." The next sentence already names the two response shapes worth attending to.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Start directly with the two possible response shapes and retain the optional skip.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
Name the artifact, not the act.
